bg-16-01.hint: It is raining, do you have an umbrella?
bg-16-01.why: 오다 attaches -는데 directly to set the background before asking a question.

bg-16-01.q: Write one sentence setting the background that you are going to the bookstore now, using 서점에 and 가는데.
bg-16-01.why: Attach -는데 to action verb 가다 to introduce the situation before asking a question.

bg-16-01.hint: Verbs ending in ㄹ drop ㄹ before -는데: 살다 → 사는데.
bg-16-01.why: Before ㄴ in -는데, the final consonant ㄹ drops from 살-: 사는데.

base.en: Would you like to go together?

steps.en: I am going to the restaurant, would you like to go together?
I am going to the restaurant right now, would you like to go together?

ko: 저는 지금 도서관에서 한국어 책을 읽는데 모르는 단어가 많아요.
옆자리에 앉은 친구에게 단어 뜻을 물어봤어요.
친구가 친절하게 설명해 주는데 이해하기 쉬웠어요.
en: I am reading a Korean book at the library right now, and there are many words I do not know.
I asked my friend sitting next to me for the meanings of the words.
My friend explained them kindly, and it was easy to understand.

bg-16-01.q: What difficulty did the speaker have while reading the Korean book?
bg-16-01.why: The passage says '한국어 책을 읽는데 모르는 단어가 많아요' (I am reading a Korean book, and there are many unknown words).
The passage says '친구가 친절하게 설명해 주는데 이해하기 쉬웠어요' (My friend explained kindly, and it was easy to understand).

items: I can attach -는데 to action verbs to set the stage for a question or suggestion
I can drop ㄹ before -는데 with ㄹ-stem verbs like 살다 (사는데)

bg-16-02.hint: It is cold outside, so please put on a coat.
bg-16-02.why: 춥다 is a ㅂ irregular adjective, so ㅂ changes to 우 before -ㄴ데: 추운데.

bg-16-02.q: Write one sentence suggesting going for a walk because the weather is nice, using 좋은데 and 산책할까요.
bg-16-02.why: 좋다 is an adjective with a batchim, so it takes -은데: 좋은데.

steps.en: The weather is nice, shall we take a walk?
The weather is nice today, shall we take a walk?

ko: 이 카페는 가게가 작은데 분위기가 아주 따뜻해요.
오늘이 주말인데도 안이 조용해서 공부하기 좋아요.
커피 맛도 정말 좋은데 가격까지 저렴해요.
en: This cafe is small, yet the atmosphere is very warm.
Even though today is the weekend, it is quiet inside and good for studying.
The coffee tastes really good too, and the price is inexpensive.

bg-16-02.q: What is the atmosphere of the cafe like?
options: Small in size, but warm and quiet
bg-16-02.why: The passage says '가게가 작은데 분위기가 아주 따뜻해요' and '안이 조용해서 공부하기 좋아요'.

bg-16-02.q: What does the passage say about the coffee at this cafe?
options: It tastes great and is inexpensive
It is sold out on weekends
bg-16-02.why: The passage states '커피 맛도 정말 좋은데 가격까지 저렴해요' (The coffee tastes really good and the price is inexpensive).

items: I can attach -(으)ㄴ데 to adjectives and -인데 to nouns to provide background context
I can conjugate ㅂ-irregular adjectives like 춥다 and 덥다 into 추운데 and 더운데

items.en: shall we go? / should I go?

bg-16-03.hint: I have plenty of time, but I have no money.
bg-16-03.why: 많다 is an adjective with a batchim, so it takes -은데: 많은데.

bg-16-03.q: Write a polite sentence declining an invitation by saying you want to go but are busy today, using 싶은데 and 바빠요.
bg-16-03.why: -고 싶다 is an adjective form, so it attaches -은데 (싶은데) to soften a refusal.

bg-16-03.wrong: 커피를 마시고 싶는데 지금 시간이 없어요.
answers: 커피를 마시고 싶은데 지금 시간이 없어요.
커피를 마시고 싶은데 지금 시간이 없어요
bg-16-03.hint: -고 싶다 functions as an adjective with batchim ㅍ, so it takes -은데, not -는데!
bg-16-03.why: 싶다 is an adjective, so attach -은데: 마시고 싶은데.

steps.en: I want to go, but I have plans.
I want to go together, but I have plans today.

ko: 수진 씨가 오늘 저녁에 삼겹살을 먹으러 가자고 했어요.
저도 정말 가고 싶은데 오늘 저녁에는 가족 모임이 있어요.
그래서 수진 씨에게 미안하다고 말하고 내일 점심에 만나기로 했어요.
en: Sujin suggested going out to eat pork belly this evening.
I really want to go too, but I have a family gathering tonight.
So I told Sujin I was sorry and we decided to meet for lunch tomorrow.

bg-16-03.q: Why can't the speaker join Sujin this evening?
options: Because they have a family gathering tonight
Because they do not like pork belly
Because they have to work overtime
bg-16-03.why: The passage says '정말 가고 싶은데 오늘 저녁에는 가족 모임이 있어요' (I really want to go, but I have a family gathering tonight).

bg-16-03.q: When did they decide to meet instead?
bg-16-03.why: The passage states '내일 점심에 만나기로 했어요' (We decided to meet for lunch tomorrow).

items: I can soften refusals and suggestions using -고 싶은데
I can contrast two situations gently using -는데 and -(으)ㄴ데

bg-16-04.hint: I am a little busy right now...
bg-16-04.why: Ending a sentence with -ㄴ데요 softens a refusal politely without sounding blunt.

bg-16-04.q: Write one sentence politely prefacing a question by saying you have a question, using 질문이 and 있는데.
bg-16-04.sample: 선생님, 질문이 있는데 잠시 시간 괜찮으세요?
bg-16-04.why: 있다 always takes -는데 (있는데) to set up a polite request or question.

bg-16-04.wrong: 식당이 여기서 조금 멀은데 택시를 탈까요?
answers: 식당이 여기서 조금 먼데 택시를 탈까요?
식당이 여기서 조금 먼데 택시를 탈까요
bg-16-04.hint: 멀다 is a ㄹ-stem adjective: drop ㄹ and attach -ㄴ데 directly!
bg-16-04.why: For ㄹ-stem adjectives like 멀다, ㄹ drops before -ㄴ데: 먼데.

steps.en: It is a bit far, shall we take the bus?
That place is a bit far, shall we take the bus?

ko: 관광객이 서울역에 가고 싶은데 길을 잘 몰랐어요.
지나가는 사람에게 길을 찾고 있는데 지하철역이 어디냐고 물어봤어요.
그 사람이 여기서 걸어가면 조금 먼데 버스를 타라고 친절하게 알려 주었어요.
en: A tourist wanted to go to Seoul Station, but did not know the way well.
They told a passerby they were looking for the way and asked where the subway station was.
The person kindly advised taking a bus since walking from here is a bit far.

bg-16-04.q: Where did the tourist want to go?
bg-16-04.why: The passage says '관광객이 서울역에 가고 싶은데 길을 잘 몰랐어요' (The tourist wanted to go to Seoul Station).

bg-16-04.q: Why did the passerby recommend taking a bus?
options: Because walking from there is a bit far
Because the subway was closed for repairs
bg-16-04.why: The passage states '여기서 걸어가면 조금 먼데 버스를 타라고 친절하게 알려 주었어요' (Walking from here is a bit far, so take a bus).

items: I can use sentence-final -는데요 / -(으)ㄴ데요 to decline invitations gently
I can conjugate 있다/없다 (있는데/없는데) and ㄹ adjectives (먼데) accurately
